AlreadyAddedResponse.description:
What the lookup may say about a number [BR2.3, BR4.5].

**Three fields, and the absences are the requirement.** No teacher
name, no teacher id, no batch name, no batch subject, no fee, no
enrollment id. With any of those this becomes an oracle for who
teaches whom, readable by anyone who can type a phone number
[AC1.12.2].

:ivar already_added: Whether a teacher recorded this number
:ivar display_name: The teacher-typed name to pre-fill as
    correctable, or None
:ivar role: The role to lock the form to, or None
AlreadyAddedResponse.title: AlreadyAddedResponse

AnnouncementBodyRequest.description:
Post or edit a note.

:ivar body: What it says
AnnouncementBodyRequest.title: AnnouncementBodyRequest

AnnouncementResponse.description:
One visible announcement.

``edited`` is the DECISION the server computes from
``edited_at``'s non-null-ness [AC3.3.2]; the timestamp itself does
not cross the wire, so there is no second source of truth for a
client to disagree with.

**No expiry field**, because there is no expiry [AC3.3.4].

:ivar announcement_id: The note
:ivar body: What it says
:ivar created_at: When it was posted
:ivar edited: Whether it has been edited
AnnouncementResponse.title: AnnouncementResponse

AttendanceEntryResponse.description:
One past session, as a student or guardian sees it.

:ivar session_id: The session
:ivar date: When it met
:ivar start_time: When it started
:ivar topic: What was covered, or null if never logged
:ivar topic_logged: Whether a topic was ever written
:ivar present: What was recorded for THIS seat, or null
:ivar subject_name: What the class taught, or null
AttendanceEntryResponse.title: AttendanceEntryResponse

AttendanceSubmitRequest.description:
A whole roster, written in one atomic operation [BR3.5].

**One of exactly two D4 bodies carrying ``client_mutation_id``**
[§ B.7]. ``base_attendance_version`` travels in the BODY rather
than an ``If-Match`` header [§ B.8]: a queued write is serialized
into the device's queue and replayed hours later by a sync worker,
and a body field survives that naturally where a header is a
second thing the queue must remember and the first thing a retry
wrapper drops.

``composed_at`` is the DEVICE's clock, recorded for the pilot's
queue-latency question and **used in no decision** [NFR24.20]. A
device clock in a conflict rule would let a wrong phone time
silently reorder two teachers' writes.

:ivar base_attendance_version: The version this was composed
    against
:ivar client_mutation_id: The replay key, per account
:ivar seats: One mark per seat, the whole roster at once
:ivar composed_at: When the device composed it, or null
AttendanceSubmitRequest.title: AttendanceSubmitRequest

AttendanceSubmitResponse.description:
What an accepted or replayed roster write produced.

**No ``queue_state`` field** [BR3.9]: the server returns the
applied version, and the client derives its own state.

:ivar attendance_version: The version now in force
:ivar submission_id: The accepted write's record
AttendanceSubmitResponse.title: AttendanceSubmitResponse

BandResponse.description:
One published band of the distribution.

Holds a **count, never a membership**. Both bounds inclusive.

:ivar low: The lowest mark in the band
:ivar high: The highest mark in the band
:ivar count: How many marked results fall in it
BandResponse.title: BandResponse

BatchCreateRequest.description:
Create a batch [AC2.1.1, AC2.1.2].

:ivar name: The teacher's name for the class
:ivar schedule: The weekly classes, so a batch can be created with its
    class days and sessions follow at once; optional
:ivar subjects: One or more subjects taught
:ivar teacher_display_name: What students see the teacher called
:ivar default_fee: The fee an enrollment inherits when it sets none
:ivar fee_due_day: Day of month 1-31; 29-31 clamp at generation
:ivar collection_number: Where payments are sent
:ivar collection_channel: Which service that number belongs to
BatchCreateRequest.title: BatchCreateRequest

BatchResponse.description:
A batch as its owner sees it.

:ivar id: The batch
:ivar name: The teacher's name for the class
:ivar subjects: The subjects taught
:ivar subject_options: The same subjects with their keys, in the same
    order, for the writes that name one
:ivar schedule: The weekly classes, in weekday then time order -- the
    "Mon Wed · 4:00 pm" line on the batch list (T6)
:ivar teacher_display_name: What students see the teacher called
:ivar default_fee: The inherited fee
:ivar fee_due_day: Day of month 1-31
:ivar collection_number: Where payments are sent
:ivar collection_channel: Which service that number belongs to
:ivar marksheet_visible: U6's toggle
:ivar active: False means read-only history
:ivar enrollment_count: How many seats, computed server-side. The
    **denominator** of "9 of 12 accepted", and it counts every seat
    the teacher created including declined ones [BR1.4]
:ivar accepted_count: How many of those seats at least one link has
    accepted [BR1.2], computed server-side and **never counted by
    the client** [BR1.3, TC-9]. A client counting rows is a client
    deciding what counts as accepted, and it is wrong the moment the
    roster paginates because it can only count the rows it holds
BatchResponse.title: BatchResponse

BatchUpdateRequest.description:
Edit a batch [AC2.3.1].

Every field optional, because a PATCH names only what changes.

:ivar name: The teacher's name for the class
:ivar subjects: The full list of subjects to keep; one with an exam
    cannot be left out
:ivar teacher_display_name: What students see the teacher called
:ivar default_fee: The inherited fee, for cycles not yet generated
:ivar fee_due_day: Day of month 1-31
:ivar collection_number: Where payments are sent
:ivar collection_channel: Which service that number belongs to
:ivar marksheet_visible: U6's toggle
:ivar active: False collapses the batch to read-only history
BatchUpdateRequest.title: BatchUpdateRequest

ClaimQueueItemResponse.description:
One claim waiting for the teacher (T4).

**The comparison is the server's.** ``comparison`` and
``difference`` are measured against what the period CHARGED
[BR5.3]; the client shows them and never subtracts.

:ivar claim_id: The claim
:ivar enrollment_id: The seat it is against
:ivar display_name: The student, as the teacher typed the name
:ivar batch_name: The batch
:ivar period: The period the claim resolved to
:ivar claimed_amount: What the payer says they sent
:ivar charged: What that period charged
:ivar comparison: ``matches``, ``short`` or ``over``
:ivar difference: How far from the charge, never negative
:ivar channel: The service the money moved through
:ivar transaction_id: The reference quoted, if any
:ivar submitted_at: When it was sent
:ivar submitted_by: ``student`` or ``guardian``, or null
:ivar submitter_phone: The number the teacher holds for them
:ivar duplicate_of: The earlier claim quoting the same reference
ClaimQueueItemResponse.title: ClaimQueueItemResponse

ClaimResponse.description:
A claim and its decision, as its submitter sees it.

``previous_decision`` is carried deliberately: a corrected
verification is visible to the teacher **and** to that student and
guardian, never hidden from either party [BR5.7, FR9.2]. It is typed
as a map of strings because every value in it -- including the
amount -- is a string, so a money value inside it crosses the wire
under the same rule as every other [BR6.2].

:ivar claim_id: The claim
:ivar period: The period it resolved to at submission
:ivar claimed_amount: What was claimed
:ivar approved_amount: What was accepted, or null while pending
:ivar status: One of the four server-set values
:ivar shortfall_disposition: Carried or waived, where one applies
:ivar channel: Which service the money moved through
:ivar submitted_at: When it was submitted
:ivar verified_at: When it was decided, or null
:ivar previous_decision: The prior decision, on a correction
ClaimResponse.title: ClaimResponse

ClaimSubmitRequest.description:
Submit a payment claim [AC6.1.x].

``claimed_amount`` is **not capped** at the outstanding balance
[BR5.2]: money may genuinely have been overpaid out of band, and
blocking that at submission makes a real overpayment unreportable.
Zero and negative are refused, which the wire pattern already does
for a negative since it admits no sign.

:ivar claimed_amount: What the claimant says they paid
:ivar channel: Which service it moved through, from the server set
:ivar transaction_id: The reference they quote, if any
ClaimSubmitRequest.title: ClaimSubmitRequest

CorrectionEntryResponse.description:
One row in a seat's correction history [FR9.2].

:ivar mark_id: The row
:ivar result_state: What it recorded
:ivar marks: Its number, or null
:ivar recorded_at: When it was entered
:ivar superseded: Whether a later row replaced it
CorrectionEntryResponse.title: CorrectionEntryResponse

CurrentFeeResponse.description:
A seat's latest fee period, as the student sees it on S1.

The status is the server's [TC-9]; the app renders it and decides
nothing from the amounts.

:ivar period: ``YYYY-MM``
:ivar status: The period's status
:ivar due_date: When it is due
:ivar outstanding: What is still owed for it
:ivar charged: What the period charged ("October fee · ৳1,200")
:ivar verifying: Whether a payment for it is waiting to be checked
:ivar paid_on: The day the last approved payment for it was
    decided, in Bangladesh, or null
CurrentFeeResponse.title: CurrentFeeResponse

DecisionResponse.description:
The seat's state after this holder decided [BR5.2].

Reports **this holder's own** decision. The other link's state is
deliberately absent: it belongs to another person, and a seat whose
student and guardian are different people shows each state only to
its own holder. The teacher's roster is where both appear side by
side, and that screen is D2's [AC1.10.7].

:ivar enrollment_id: The seat decided on
:ivar decision: This holder's decision after the write
DecisionResponse.title: DecisionResponse

DeletionOutcome.description:
What the external route did: sent a code, or deleted.

The two values are the two steps, and nothing distinguishes a known
number from an unknown one within either. A second request for an
account already deleted returns ``deleted`` [BR1.4]: on a deletion
screen an error reads as "it did not work", and the action already
succeeded.

:ivar status: ``requested`` after a code is sent, ``deleted``
    after one is spent
DeletionOutcome.title: DeletionOutcome

DeletionRequest.description:
Ask for a deletion code, or confirm with one.

**``code`` is optional and that is what selects the step.** The
external route is one route with two steps rather than two routes,
because ``PUBLIC_ROUTES`` declares exactly two external deletion
entries and asserts its own count -- a separate code endpoint would
be a ninth public route [BR3.2].

:ivar phone: The number whose account is to be deleted
:ivar code: The deletion code, or None to be sent one

phone.description: A Bangladeshi mobile number. Any common spelling is accepted (01711234567, 01711-234567, +8801711234567, Bangla digits); it is stored and returned as +8801XXXXXXXXX.
phone.title: Phone

DeletionRequest.title: DeletionRequest

DeletionResponse.description:
The in-app acknowledgement.

A distinct model from :class:`DeletionOutcome` because the in-app
route has exactly one outcome: it is authenticated, so there is no
code step. Carrying the two-valued model here would publish a
``requested`` the route can never return.

**No row counts and no ``existed`` flag**, however useful they would
be to a client. The in-app route could afford one -- the caller is
authenticated -- and does not take one anyway: two shapes for one
outcome is how the paths start to drift [BR3.1].

:ivar status: Always ``deleted``
DeletionResponse.title: DeletionResponse

DeletionSummaryResponse.description:
What stays after this account is deleted, for the confirm screen.

Zeros for anyone who owns no batch: the screen then shows the plain
variant rather than a refusal.

:ivar batch_count: Batches the account owns
:ivar student_count: Students in them
:ivar outstanding: What those students still owe; it stays on their
    records and can no longer be collected
DeletionSummaryResponse.title: DeletionSummaryResponse

DuesGroupResponse.description:
One group on the Dues screen, totalled by the server.

:ivar bucket: Which group: more than 30 days late, 1-30 days late,
    or due and not yet late
:ivar total: What its rows owe together
:ivar count: How many rows
:ivar share: Its total as a whole percent of everything owed, so the
    app draws the bar without dividing money
DuesGroupResponse.title: DuesGroupResponse

DuesResponse.description:
Everyone who owes this teacher money, across every batch.

**An empty ``rows`` is the defined empty state** [BR1.5], never a
404 and never an error: a teacher whose students have all paid is
getting the best possible news, and a failure shape would make the
app render a retry prompt for it.

:ivar summary: The totals, overall and per group
:ivar rows: One entry per owing seat, latest debt first, possibly
    empty
DuesResponse.title: DuesResponse

DuesRowResponse.description:
One person who owes money, in one batch [FR7.1].

The key is ``enrollment_id`` and never an account id [ADR-001], and
``display_name`` is the TEACHER's record rather than anything the
student or guardian wrote [TC-13]. Both are asserted schema-wide by
the built privacy gate rather than by remembering it here.

:ivar enrollment_id: The teacher-facing key
:ivar batch_id: The batch the debt sits in
:ivar batch_name: That batch's name, because the same person may
    owe in two
:ivar display_name: The teacher-typed name
:ivar outstanding: What this seat still owes
:ivar oldest_unpaid_period: Which period the debt starts in, or
    null
:ivar latest_unpaid_period: Which period it runs to, or null
:ivar days_late: Days since the oldest late due date, or null when
    nothing is past due
:ivar bucket: Which group the row belongs in
:ivar last_reminded_at: When a reminder last went out, if ever
:ivar remindable: Whether "Remind" would reach this seat now
DuesRowResponse.title: DuesRowResponse

DuesSummaryResponse.description:
The Dues screen's headline, so the app adds up nothing [TC-9].

:ivar total: Everything owed
:ivar count: How many seats owe it
:ivar late_total: What is owed past its due date
:ivar remindable: How many seats a "Remind" would reach
:ivar groups: One per bucket, latest first, empty ones included
DuesSummaryResponse.title: DuesSummaryResponse

DuplicateClaimResponse.description:
The earlier claim that quoted the same transaction id.

:ivar claim_id: That claim
:ivar display_name: Whose seat it was on, as the teacher typed it
:ivar status: How it was decided
:ivar amount: What was approved, else what was claimed
:ivar decided_at: When it was decided, or null
DuplicateClaimResponse.title: DuplicateClaimResponse

EnrollmentCreateRequest.description:
Add a student to a batch [AC2.2.2, AC2.2.5].

``fee_amount`` is nullable and null means **inherit** the batch
default. Zero is a real fee of zero, which is a waiver -- a
non-nullable column defaulting to zero would make the two
indistinguishable and silently charge nothing.

:ivar display_name: The teacher-typed name for this seat
:ivar student_phone: The student's number, typed by the teacher
:ivar guardian_phone: The guardian's number, if one is recorded
:ivar fee_amount: This seat's fee, or null to inherit
:ivar joined_on: When the student joined

anyOf.description: A Bangladeshi mobile number. Any common spelling is accepted (01711234567, 01711-234567, +8801711234567, Bangla digits); it is stored and returned as +8801XXXXXXXXX.

ExamCreateRequest.description:
Create or edit an assessment [BR4.1].

:ivar batch_subject_id: One of the batch's own subjects
:ivar title: The teacher's name for it
:ivar date: When it was sat
:ivar total_marks: The denominator, at least 1
ExamCreateRequest.title: ExamCreateRequest

ExamListItemResponse.description:
One exam on the teacher's list, with its marking progress.

Counted server-side, so the client never tallies a rows list to
decide what counts as entered.

:ivar entered_count: Seats with a mark or an absence entered
:ivar expected_count: Seats that could have sat the exam
:ivar state: ``upcoming``, ``needs_marks`` or ``complete``, decided
    by the server so the client never compares a date or a count
ExamListItemResponse.title: ExamListItemResponse

ExamResponse.description:
One assessment.

:ivar exam_id: The exam
:ivar title: The teacher's name for it
:ivar date: When it was sat
:ivar total_marks: The denominator, an integer COUNT
:ivar subject_name: The subject assessed
ExamResponse.title: ExamResponse

ExamResultsResponse.description:
One exam's results, with the exam and whether it may be written.

**A wrapper rather than a bare array, and `writable` is why.** The
screen must know whether to offer mark entry at all, and that is a
server decision [BR5.5]: an exam in an inactive batch is read-only
and the write is refused with `teaching.batch.inactive`. Without
it the client either guesses, or offers an entry field that fails
on save — which is the failure a person blames on the app.

The exam travels with the results because the screen shows its
title and total alongside them, and a second request to learn what
the first was about is a round trip the server can spare.

:ivar exam: The exam these results belong to
:ivar results: One row per seat [BR4.3]
:ivar writable: Whether marks may be entered, decided server-side
ExamResultsResponse.title: ExamResultsResponse

ExamUpdateRequest.description:
Edit an assessment: what it is called, when, and out of how much.

No subject: an edit names what changes, and the exam stays in the
subject it was set in.

:ivar title: The teacher's name for it
:ivar date: When it was sat
:ivar total_marks: The denominator, at least 1, and not below any
    mark already recorded
ExamUpdateRequest.title: ExamUpdateRequest

FamilyBatchViewResponse.description:
What a student or guardian sees of one batch [BR7.2].

``served_at`` is BR7.3's server timestamp, so a client rendering
this from cache can state its age without consulting the device
clock -- which is the thing excluded from decisions.

:ivar next_session_date: The next scheduled session's date, or
    null
:ivar next_session_start_time: Its start time, or null
:ivar past_sessions: Past sessions with topics and attendance
:ivar announcements: The batch's visible notes
:ivar served_at: When the server computed this
:ivar next_session: The next class, or null
:ivar following_sessions: The classes after it, soonest first
:ivar upcoming_exam: The next exam still to be sat, or null
FamilyBatchViewResponse.title: FamilyBatchViewResponse

FeeCycleResponse.description:
One period's fee, for any lens entitled to read it.

``status`` is the decision; ``outstanding`` is reported for display
and is never what the client computes a status from.

:ivar period: The period, as ``YYYY-MM``
:ivar due_date: The due date, after the short-month clamp
:ivar charged: What was charged for this period
:ivar outstanding: What is still owed, floored at zero
:ivar status: The server-computed status
FeeCycleResponse.title: FeeCycleResponse

FeeHistoryResponse.description:
One seat's periods, with the total the server computed.

**A wrapper rather than a bare array, and the total is why.** The
client must not sum the rows: that is money arithmetic on the
Android side, which [D-20] forbids, and it would be wrong the
moment the history paginates — a page of three periods would
report a total that is not the balance.

The value is the ledger fold's own ``total_outstanding``, floored
at zero inside the money module, not a second sum computed beside
the rows.

:ivar cycles: One row per generated period, oldest first
:ivar total_outstanding: What this seat still owes in total
FeeHistoryResponse.title: FeeHistoryResponse

GuardianChildResponse.description:
One reachable child as a guardian sees it.

Carries ``batch_name`` and ``teacher_display_name`` because
attribution is required even in the single-child case [AC2.8.5] --
that is where it is most needed, since the selection list is where
it would otherwise have been shown.

:ivar enrollment_id: The seat, which BR5.1 keys the route on
:ivar display_name: The teacher-typed name for the child
:ivar batch_name: Which class
:ivar teacher_display_name: Which teacher recorded this
GuardianChildResponse.title: GuardianChildResponse

HealthResponse.description:
What the smoke set reads.

:ivar status: ``ok`` when the process is serving
:ivar database: ``ok`` or ``fail``
:ivar migration_revision: The applied Alembic revision, or None
HealthResponse.title: HealthResponse

InactiveFromRequest.description:
Mark a seat inactive from a date, or clear it [AC2.4.1].

:ivar inactive_from: The date, or null to reactivate the seat
InactiveFromRequest.title: InactiveFromRequest

InboxResponse.description:
The reader's inbox, newest first.

:ivar items: The messages
:ivar unread: How many have not been seen, over the whole inbox
InboxResponse.title: InboxResponse

InvitationResponse.description:
One unaccepted seat, in exactly the width BR1.4 permits.

Batch name, subject and fee amount -- all teacher-authored, so this
read crosses no privacy boundary -- plus the seat's own id, which
the accept and decline routes are keyed on, and this holder's own
decision so the screen can offer the right action without deciding
what ``declined`` means for itself [TC-9].

**There is no attendance, no mark, no other enrollment and no
further batch field**, and no write action but accept and decline
on the link that names the holder [AC1.10.2].

:ivar enrollment_id: The seat, which the decision routes are keyed on
:ivar batch_name: The class being joined
:ivar subject: The subjects taught, as the teacher named them
:ivar fee_amount: This seat's fee, or None when it inherits the
    batch default. None is NOT zero: zero is a waiver
:ivar decision: This holder's own decision, ``pending`` or
    ``declined``
:ivar role: Which link this account holds on the seat. Present
    because the DECLINE CONFIRMATION differs by role [BR5.2]: a
    student's decline stops their fee, a guardian's leaves the
    student's obligation entirely intact. The client had no
    trustworthy way to tell them apart, and one confirmation shown
    to both told a guardian a debt was cancelled when it was not.

    This discloses nothing new -- the holder is on this seat -- and
    it is decided server-side rather than inferred from a lens hint
    the client supplied [TC-11, D-2]
InvitationResponse.title: InvitationResponse

IssueRequest.description:
Ask for a code to be sent to a number.

The number is **typed by the user** and never read from the SIM
[AC1.1.6]: there is no device-side source for this field.

:ivar phone: The destination number in international form

phone.description: A Bangladeshi mobile number. Any common spelling is accepted (01711234567, 01711-234567, +8801711234567, Bangla digits); it is stored and returned as +8801XXXXXXXXX.
phone.title: Phone

IssueRequest.title: IssueRequest

IssueResponse.description:
The response to an issue request, for **any** number.

One field, and it is a fixed string. Anything varying between the
known and unknown branches -- a count, a timestamp, a message -- is
the existence oracle re-entering through the schema.

:ivar status: Always ``requested``
IssueResponse.title: IssueResponse

LastResultResponse.description:
A student's latest marked result in one batch ("Last test 44/50").

:ivar title: The exam
:ivar marks: The mark
:ivar total_marks: Out of how many
:ivar rank: The rank, only where the marksheet publishes it
LastResultResponse.title: LastResultResponse

LensEntry.description:
One lens the account can choose.

:ivar kind: Which lens: teacher, student or guardian
:ivar count: How much sits behind it
LensEntry.title: LensEntry

MarkWriteRequest.description:
Enter or correct one seat's result [BR4.2].

**No version field**: a mark is an interactive write and cannot
conflict [BR3.11].

``marks`` is non-null if and only if ``result_state`` is
``marked``. A zero IS a mark: a zero stored as ``absent`` tells a
guardian their child missed an exam they sat and failed.

:ivar enrollment_id: The seat
:ivar result_state: ``marked`` or ``absent``
:ivar marks: The number, or null
MarkWriteRequest.title: MarkWriteRequest

MarksheetToggleRequest.description:
Set whether families may see a marksheet [BR5.4].

:ivar visible: Whether families may see it
MarksheetToggleRequest.title: MarksheetToggleRequest

MeResponse.description:
Everything this account can be.

**No role, and no default lens.** The list says what is available;
which one the person wants is their choice, and a server-chosen
default would be a stored role by another name. A single-entry
list is the app's cue to skip the picker.

:ivar lenses: Every available lens, teacher first
:ivar self_name: The name this person chose for themselves, or
    None before they have set one
:ivar address: Their address, or None. **Owner-private** [BR3.4]:
    it sits in `OWNER_PRIVATE_FIELDS` and reaches no teacher-lens
    response, which the schema-wide privacy gate asserts. It is
    returned HERE because this is the owner reading their own row
:ivar phone: The number this account signs in with. The owner's own
    login, read by the owner on a lens-exempt route; the profile
    shows it read-only, and in-app deletion asks the person to type
    it back as confirmation, which needs the app to know it
MeResponse.title: MeResponse

Money.description: A BDT amount in canonical form: exactly two decimal places, no thousands separator, no currency symbol, no sign. Always a JSON string, never a JSON number.
Money.title: Money

MonthlyEarningsResponse.description:
Money received in one calendar month [FR8.1].

:ivar period: The month, as ``YYYY-MM``
:ivar received: ``receipt`` plus ``credit_grant`` for that month
MonthlyEarningsResponse.title: MonthlyEarningsResponse

NextExamResponse.description:
The soonest exam dated today or later [FR8.4].

:ivar exam_id: The exam
:ivar title: The teacher's name for it
:ivar batch_name: Which class sits it
:ivar subject_name: The subject assessed
:ivar date: When it is sat
:ivar days_remaining: Whole days, computed server-side [BR3.2] --
    a client computing it would use the device clock and would
    disagree across time zones
NextExamResponse.title: NextExamResponse

NotificationResponse.description:
One message in the reader's own inbox.

:ivar notification_id: The message
:ivar kind: What produced it
:ivar enrollment_id: The seat it is about, if any
:ivar batch_name: The batch, as named when it was sent
:ivar period: The period it concerns, as ``YYYY-MM``, if any
:ivar amount: The money it concerns, if any
:ivar created_at: When it was sent
:ivar read: Whether the reader has opened the inbox since
NotificationResponse.title: NotificationResponse

OutstandingResponse.description:
What students owe across every batch, and how much is late (T1).

**``overdue`` is the server's decision**: owing on a period whose
due date has passed in Bangladesh. The client never compares a due
date with its clock.

:ivar batch_count: Batches with anything owing

OverviewResponse.description:
The three blocks of the teacher overview, each independently absent.

**``earnings`` is never absent and ``trend`` and ``next_exam``
may be**, which is the distinction this model exists to publish:

* ``earnings`` carries a **zero value** in a month with no receipts
  [BR2.2]. Rendering zero as "no data" tells a teacher their records
  are missing when they are complete, in the month they most need to
  know the number is really zero;
* ``trend`` is **null under two months of history** [BR2.3], not a
  one-point series -- a single point implies a direction it cannot
  know;
* ``next_exam`` is **null when nothing is scheduled** [BR3.4], which
  the client renders as a defined empty state rather than a failure.

:ivar earnings: This month's money received; never absent
:ivar trend: The monthly series ascending, or null under two months
:ivar next_exam: The soonest upcoming exam, or null

**The ONE response in the product carrying the collection number**
[BR6.4, NFR14.32]. The allowlist test asserts that as an equality
against a one-element set, so the field spreading to a second
response fails the build rather than passing a membership check.

Where the teacher set no number the route returns **no object at
all** rather than this model with a null in it [NFR14.34]: a null
invites a client-side placeholder, and an absent object leaves the
client nothing to render while the copy tells the person to ask the
teacher how to pay.

and it cannot touch a lens: a role is computed per request from
owned batches and enrollments and has no stored field to set

One seat's fee position, as its teacher sees it.

The key is ``enrollment_id`` and never an account id [ADR-001],
asserted schema-wide by the built privacy gate.

**No ``collection_number``.** The teacher's payment destination is
carried by exactly one response and this is not it [NFR14.33].

:ivar display_name: The teacher-typed name

:ivar due_date: That period's due date, or null

RosterRowResponse.description:
One seat as a teacher sees it.

``status`` is a **server-computed decision**, not an input to one
[TC-9]: the client switches on this enum and never compares a date
or an amount of its own.

:ivar enrollment_id: The teacher-facing key for this seat
:ivar display_name: The teacher-typed name
:ivar guardian_phone: The teacher-typed guardian contact
:ivar fee_amount: This seat's fee, or null when it inherits
:ivar status: ``dormant``, ``active`` or ``inactive``.

    **Unchanged, and the two new fields sit beside it rather than
    replacing it.** Acceptance is a different axis from activity:
    an inactive seat keeps whatever decisions its links carry,
    because leaving a batch is not un-accepting it. Folding the two
    together would produce a product of two axes and a value set
    nobody can switch on exhaustively
:ivar student_state: The student link's own decision --
    ``pending``, ``accepted`` or ``declined`` [BR2.1]
:ivar guardian_state: The guardian link's own decision, plus
    ``absent`` when no guardian was recorded [BR2.2]. ``absent`` is
    a fourth VALUE and not a null, because a decision nobody was
    asked for is not an outstanding one
:ivar is_removable: Whether removal would succeed [BR3.1].

    **A decision the client reads and never derives** [NFR14.31].
    Removal tests two conditions -- no link accepted, and no erasure
    marker set -- and this row carries only the first. A client
    inferring removability from the link states it displays would
    offer the action on an erased seat, which is a wrong answer
    presented as an available action rather than a style violation
:ivar inactive_from: The recorded date, if any
RosterRowResponse.title: RosterRowResponse

RosterSeatResponse.description:
One seat on a session's roster.

The key is ``enrollment_id`` and never an account id [ADR-001,
BR5.3], asserted schema-wide by the built privacy gate.

``present`` is **null where nothing was recorded**, which is a
different fact from ``false``: AC3.1.4 defaults every seat to
present in the UI and the teacher marks only exceptions, so
collapsing the two would tell a guardian their child was marked
absent from a class nobody has marked at all.

:ivar enrollment_id: The teacher-facing key
:ivar display_name: The TEACHER-typed name
:ivar present: What was recorded, or null

One seat's result, as its TEACHER sees it.

and a teacher already knows who is in their own class. The

:ivar start_time: Its new start time

One session, for any lens entitled to read it.

Attendance writes carry a `base_attendance_version` and a stale
one is refused with a 409 [TC-8, D-9]. After that refusal the app
re-reads the roster to show what changed — and without the current
version here it cannot compose the next write, so a conflict
becomes a dead end rather than something a person can resolve.

VerificationRequest.description:
Record a teacher's decision on a claim [AC6.3.x].

``shortfall_disposition`` is **required where the approval is below
the charge and forbidden where it is not** [BR5.4]. It carries no
default: the two choices have opposite consequences for the student,
so a default silently chooses for the teacher. The requirement
cannot be expressed in the schema alone -- it depends on what the
cycle was charged -- so the server enforces it and this field stays
optional here.

``correcting`` is **the teacher saying "I know this claim is already
decided and I am revising it"** [BR5.7, FR9.2]. It defaults to
``False``, so an ordinary verification of an undecided claim needs no
flag and a *concurrent* second verification is refused rather than
silently double-crediting the payment.

It cannot be inferred from the claim's state. A decided claim with a
second request arriving is exactly the shape of both the race this
guard exists to stop and the correction FR9.2 requires, and the
server cannot tell them apart -- only the teacher knows which one
they meant. Inferring it would mean choosing to let the race through.

:ivar approved_amount: What the teacher accepts
:ivar shortfall_disposition: Carried or waived, where one applies
:ivar correcting: True when deliberately revising a decided claim
VerificationRequest.title: VerificationRequest

get.description:
Serve the externally reachable deletion page.

No session, no database read and no parameters: it is a static page
whose only job is to be reachable and to name the app and developer
[AC1.7.2].

:return: The page

post.description:
Send a deletion code, or delete once one is presented.

**One route with two steps rather than two routes**, and that is a
deliberate consequence of the allowlist rather than a convenience.
``PUBLIC_ROUTES`` declares exactly two external deletion entries,
its count is asserted at eight, and D6's stated job is to land
handlers against entries already under review -- not to add a public
route in the commit that implements one. A separate
``/account-deletion/code`` would have been a ninth public entry,
which is a diff against a stated number [BR3.2].

The step is chosen by whether ``code`` is present, which is also how
the page's single form behaves: submit a number to be sent a code,
submit it again with the code to confirm.

``verify`` is CALLED rather than reimplemented, which is what gives
this route the single-use rule, the expiry and the attempt ceiling
without a second copy of any of them [NFR14.81]. Reimplementing it
is the obvious shortcut for a route living in a different module.

:param body: The request body
:param request: The incoming request
:param session: The request-scoped session
:param gateway: The configured SMS gateway
:return: ``requested`` after a code is sent, ``deleted`` after one
    is spent
:raises CeilingBreach: A deletion ceiling refused this send
:raises ValidationError: The code is wrong, expired, used or was
    issued for a different purpose

post.description:
Create an account, then send the verification code [BR4.3].

**The ordering is the requirement, not an implementation detail**
[AC1.11.4]. The account exists before the code is sent, so a person
who verifies always has something to verify into; sending first
would mean a code arriving for an account that may never be
created.

The ceiling is consumed **before** the account is created, for the
reason the OTP path checks before its gateway call: a ceiling
checked afterwards has already spent what it exists to protect.

Public by design, and in ``PUBLIC_ROUTES``: there is no session to
authenticate with before an account exists.

:param body: The signup request
:param request: The incoming request
:param session: The request-scoped session
:param gateway: The configured SMS gateway
:return: The new account and the number its code went to
:raises CeilingBreach: A signup ceiling refused this request
:raises DuplicateNumber: The number already has an account

get.description:
Report whether a teacher recorded this number, and nothing more.

**This route discloses that a seat exists, deliberately**
[BR2.3, AC1.12.2]. That is its purpose, and it is why BR2.2's
byte-identical requirement applies to the OTP endpoint and not to
this one. What is bounded is the WIDTH -- never the teacher, never
the batch -- and the rate, through signup's own ceilings.

Public, and in ``PUBLIC_ROUTES``: it is called while the signup
form renders, before any account exists.

:param phone: The number typed into the form, canonicalised on the
    way in like every other number, so the ceiling and the lookup
    both see one spelling
:param request: The incoming request
:param session: The request-scoped session
:return: Existence, the name to pre-fill and the role to lock
:raises CeilingBreach: A signup ceiling refused this request
